note: OBSERVED gate runtimes in ms. Written by tools/ship/selfchecks.mjs on a full run and read by gateBudget-selfcheck, which compares the recorded SLOWEST_GENERAL against what was actually seen. IT SHIPS WITH DATA rather than empty: a check fed by a file nobody has produced is a control that cannot fail, and this one exists precisely because the previous budget rule lived in a comment.
captured: v3211 full-suite run (556 gates) plus the quiet-box tail measured with a 300s ceiling; plus 13 gates added in the v3285 session, each timed individually on this box (not batch wall-clock -- the first pass through this round attached the word MEASURED to estimates that a re-measure contradicted by up to 20x); plus the 15 gates added v3567-v3583, EACH TIMED INDIVIDUALLY on this box following the v3285 precedent rather than batch wall-clock. placementRender was timed WITH jsdom INSTALLED (7.6s): without it the gate SKIPS in 39ms, and recording a skip as a runtime would have put a 39ms budget on a 7.6s check. ; plus 24 gates timed individually at v3924 -- the clean-passing part of a 55-gate sweep of everything that had NEITHER a recorded time NOR a MEASURED budget. Twelve of those 55 exceeded a 150s cap and are NOT here: a gate that does not complete leaves no entry, which is the reason this file could never show an over-budget gate and why 'zero over default' was a property of the file rather than of the tree. Nineteen more exited nonzero and are excluded by the same rule that has always excluded failures. ; and at v3925 placementRender was re-timed WITH jsdom PRESENT: 14057ms, replacing a recorded 54ms that was its SKIP time. The gate reports cleanly and exits 0 when jsdom is absent, so the writer recorded a measurement of the check declining to run -- 54ms as the budget for a 14s check, which the first timeout would have made look like a hang in something that is fine. jsdom is a dev dependency, npm i jsdom --no-save, as that gate's own header says.
failingNote: RUNTIMES OF GATES THAT COMPLETED AND EXITED NONZERO, recorded at v3924 and kept OUT of `timings` because the writer has always excluded failures -- a gate that fails early has not exercised its full path, so its time understates. They are recorded HERE because a red verdict is not the same fact as an unknown runtime, and folding the two together is how nineteen failing gates stayed invisible: none of them had ever been timed, so nothing in the tree had a reason to run them. THIS MAP IS EVIDENCE ABOUT DURATION, NOT A SUPPRESSION OF THE FAILURE -- the failures are real, they are listed here by name, and they are the next round's work.
